events.title: Monday briefing: ​How the Cockroach ​protests ​have expose​d the ​cracks in ​India’s government
events.summary:
In today’s newsletter: Across ​the country, a ​younger generation is turning private disillusionment into public defiance​ against a government that once felt untouchable

Good morning. As flames engulfed parts of France and Spain this weekend, in India, the prime minister, Narendra Modi, was trying to put out a very different kind of fire. Thousands of people arrived in Delhi on Saturday to demand the resignation of his education minister, Dharmendra Pradhan. When he stepped down in the early afternoon, the protests turned into a triumphant block party.

But the Cockroach protests that have swept through India this summer are about much more than a single minister. They have humiliated Modi and undermined the indomitable power of his Bharatiya Janata party (BJP) that has ruled India for the past 12 years. They’re also a lesson in using humour to political advantage.

He presents a compelling paradox: while ceasefires and pilot return zones might seem promising, recovery is not simply about returning people to their homes, but about rebuilding dignity, restoring public services, addressing invisible psychological wounds, and sustaining international solidarity over the long term. Rassi argues that resilience depends as much on sustained commitment, protection of humanitarian workers, and community trust as it does on immediate relief.

events.title: Photos show North and South Korea still divided 73 years after the armistice
events.summary:
North and South Korea remain separated by one of the world’s most heavily armed borders. It's a lasting reminder that the 1950-53 Korean War ended with an armistice, not a peace treaty, leaving the countries technically still at war. 

More than seven decades after the conflict began, its scars and impact remain visible, not only by border area fortifications and war memorials, but also in the lives of separated families and survivors who continue to carry memories of loss and longing. 

Although the fighting ended with the July 27, 1953, armistice agreement, the traces the war left behind serve as enduring reminders of the past, ensuring that history is not only remembered but passed onto future generations.

events.summary: An American eye surgeon and his team performed over 1,000 cataract surgeries in Abyei along the South Sudan border, restoring sight to thousands in a region with one of the world's highest blindness rates. NBC News' Molly Hunter reports.

events.title: Suspect killed after deadly Berlin terror attack
events.summary: Berlin police shot and killed 21-year-old Abdul Ballout after authorities say he rushed at officers with a stabbing weapon while they tried to arrest him today. Police say the suspect drove a white van into dozens of people as they walked through a park. Many of the victims were attending a large Pride event. NBC News’ Valerie Castro has the latest.

events.title: Suspect in Berlin Pride march attack shot and killed by police
events.summary: Berlin police shot and killed the suspect in the deadly attack in the city’s Pride festival after he allegedly charged at officers with a knife while they tried to arrest him, authorities said.

events.title: Suspect in deadly Berlin Pride attack is killed, according to German police
events.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and other government officials visited the scene where a vehicle was driven into a crowd near Berlin’s Pride festival, killing a woman and injuring 29 others. The suspect has been killed, according to German police.

events.title: Berlin police kill suspect in Pride festival attack after manhunt
events.summary: Authorities say the 21-year-old was fatally shot after allegedly charging at officers with a knife, a day after an attack left one dead and 29 injured.

events.title: U.S. forgoes strikes on Iran, but conflict in the Red Sea escalates
events.summary: U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” that the pause in strikes was due to ongoing talks between the two countries.

events.title: ‘Cockroaches won’: India’s youth protest leaders declare victory as minister resigns
events.summary: India’s viral Cockroach Janta Party called off its nationwide protests Saturday after the country’s education minister resigned and the government agreed to a number of the activist movement’s demands.

events.title: U.S. launches new strikes and Trump threatens ‘massive attack’ as Iran widens war
events.summary: The United States launched a fresh barrage of strikes on Iran overnight as President Donald Trump threatened a major new escalation after Tehran opened a second front in its pressure campaign on the world economy.

events.title: No basic services and nowhere to go: How Venezuelans are living a month after the earthquakes
events.summary: We visited the ruins of a housing complex built by the Chavista regime: the now homeless residents brave the heat, humidity, and flies from their tents, as they’re promised a house by 2027.

events.title: ‘Cockroach’ protests spread across India as leading activist ends hunger strike
events.summary: An activist has ended his 26-day hunger strike that galvanized India’s “Cockroach” protests, turning them into one of the biggest challenges to the government.

events.title: Oil prices surge to $100 per barrel after Red Sea attacks
events.summary: European and U.S. crude oil both jumped, hitting their highest levels in weeks.

events.title: Trump says Saudi Arabia must normalize Israel ties before nuclear deal is approved
events.summary: The president added that the deal “is totally subject to Saudi Arabia joining the very respected and successful Abraham Accords.”

events.title: U.S. signs landmark nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia
events.summary: The U.S. will support creating a civilian nuclear power program in the kingdom under the agreement, a senior administration official told NBC News.

events.title: U.S. military identifies soldiers killed in Iranian attack in Jordan
events.summary: The Pentagon identified the soldiers as 25-year-old Tyler James Feehan of Hawaii and 19-year-old Isabella Gonzales of Texas.
